beats.text: Flag number *four*.
For nearly 10 years, Texas was its own country, the Republic of Texas.
It had its own president, its own army, its own money, and not much else.
It was *broke*.
It had a war with the Comanche, a hostile Mexico, and debts it could not pay,
and its constitution protected slavery.
It even made it hard for free Black people to live there at all.
So most Texans wanted to join the United States, but up north, that was a problem.
Adding Texas meant adding a giant new slave state.
In Washington, it turned into a nine-year *brawl*.
Finally, on December the 29th, 1845, Texas became the *28th* state.
Flag number six is coming, but first, flag number five.
Annexation also started a *war*.
Texas said its border was the *Rio Grande*.
Mexico said it was the *Nueces* River, more than 100 miles north.
The United States sent troops into the gap.
The Mexican-American War followed, and by 1848, Mexico had lost not
just Texas, but California and most of the American Southwest.
Now, here is where our story really starts, because in 1840s Texas, the
dominant party was the *Democrats*.
The national Democratic Party of the time was the party of the
South, the party of expansion, and the party that defended slavery.
Remember that, because the parties we know today were about to be
born, and Texas was about to choose a side that would last a *century*.
